title: Event assertions ledger and compact changeframe format for RBAC v2 admin operations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and finalize a compact, append-only 'changeframe' event format and an assertions-ledger layer for audit events emitted by RBAC v2 admin flows (users, roles, policies, SSO bindings). Deliverables: event shape, actor/target canonicalization rules, diff encoding for config mutations, retention/redaction guidance, sampling policy, and instrumentation checklist for SDKs + ingress proxies.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document with canonical event shape and example payloads for create/update/delete and policy-eval events
Diff encoding defined with examples for nested policy changes and role bindings
List of canonical actor and target identifiers and fallbacks (user id, service principal, external SAML subject)
Backward-compatible mapping for current audit consumers (incidents dashboard, compliance export, SIEM ingestion)
Security review completed and sign-off from Security and Privacy teams
decisions: Use an append-only changeframe where each admin mutation emits: header (meta), before_digest (optional), after_digest, compact_diff (ndjson array of atomic ops), assertions (list of high-level checks)
Canonical actor identifier prioritized: (1) internal user_id, (2) oauth_client_id, (3) saml.external_subject, with clear 'actor_type' field
Store human-readable "action_summary" in event but require ingesters to derive changes from compact_diff for audit accuracy
Compact diff will adopt an operation-centric schema (op:path:type:val) to minimize payload and simplify partial redaction
Redaction strategy: PII fields replaced with deterministic tokens; sensitive keys omitted from compact_diff and appended to secure vault reference if needed
open_questions: What is the retention SLA for before_digest blobs for dedicated vs hosted customers? (ops to propose)
Should we include full pre-change snapshot for policy updates that affect > N principals? (cost vs forensic value)
How to surface cross-tenant admin actions in aggregated telemetry without exposing tenant ids?
Do we need a separate stream for high-frequency 'permission-check' telemetry vs low-frequency 'policy-change' events?

consumers_and_migration_notes: Existing consumers: incidents dashboard (queries full event), compliance export (expects JSON snapshots), SIEM (prefers key fields)
Migration plan: emit changeframe-v1 alongside current audit_v1 for 6 weeks; add a decoder lib in runtime and SDKs to translate for legacy consumers
Versioning: include ingest_version and decoder_version in headers for safe rollout
implementation_notes: Encoder will produce ndjson compact_diff entries; runtime will optionally attach before_digest only when change size < 64KB to control storage
Provide a server-side redaction hook that replaces configured sensitive field paths with deterministic tokens (tenant-scoped) and logs redaction metadata to a secure channel
Expose sampling knobs: policy_change.sample_rate (default 1.0), permission_check.sample_rate (default 0.05) with burst allowance for incident windows
Add unit tests that round-trip compact_diff -> apply -> verify after_digest equals after_digest from event
